diagnoses.description: `holding_analysis.py` ignores the `--quarter` argument when loading data: it reads `/root/INFOTABLE.tsv` instead of `/root/{quarter}/INFOTABLE.tsv`, so results can come from the wrong quarter and the quarter parameter only affects printing.

`holding_analysis.py` claims to return/print “fund managers” but only groups by and prints `ACCESSION_NUMBER` values; it never joins to `COVERPAGE.tsv` (or similar) to retrieve manager names, so it cannot actually output manager names as stated.

`one_fund_analysis.py` has a malformed `title_class_of_stocks` list due to missing commas between many string literals (Python concatenates adjacent string literals). This collapses many intended entries into a few long strings, breaking the stock-filtering logic that relies on `.isin(title_class_of_stocks)`.

`one_fund_analysis.py` reports “Total AUM” as `infotable['VALUE'].sum()`, which is the sum of reported position values in INFOTABLE, not an AUM field from fund metadata/cover page. This mislabels holdings value as AUM and can be incorrect for tasks requiring fund AUM from filing metadata.

`one_fund_analysis.py` reports “Number of stock holdings” as `stock_infotable.shape[0]` (row count). This overcounts when the same stock/CUSIP appears in multiple rows; the task-style question “how many stocks are held” typically requires a distinct CUSIP count.

locations.section: read_one_quarter_data(): print('- Number of stock holdings: ...')

diagnoses.description: `search_stock_cusip.py` hardcodes the dataset to `/root/2025-q2/INFOTABLE.tsv` and provides no quarter argument, so stock CUSIP lookup is limited to Q2 data and can fail/mislead for Q3-only securities or datasets stored only under other quarter folders.
`search_stock_cusip.py` repeats the same malformed `title_class_of_stocks` list issue (missing commas causing unintended string concatenation), making its equity filtering unreliable.
